name: auth
summary: Single-user accounts: email/password registration and login, Google OAuth sign-in, and the RequireAuth middleware that every other domain's protected routes are wrapped in. Issues stateless HS256 JWTs carrying user_id.
exposes: Handlers.RequireAuth(next http.HandlerFunc) http.HandlerFunc — the auth wrapper used by every other domain
auth.UserIDFromContext(ctx) (string, bool) — how handlers read the caller
TokenIssuer.IssueToken(userID) / VerifyToken(token) — also used directly by datasource sheets_handlers
Store methods: CreateUser, GetUserByEmail/ByID/ByGoogleID, LinkGoogleID, CreateGoogleUser
key_notes: JWT TTL is 24h (tokenTTL in jwt.go) and there is no refresh token or revocation. Logging out is purely a client-side localStorage delete.
VerifyToken explicitly rejects non-HMAC signing methods — that check guards against the alg-confusion attack, do not remove it.

users.password_hash was made nullable by migration 0002 for Google-only accounts, but auth.User.PasswordHash is a plain string, so a Google-only user's scan relies on the DB never returning NULL there in practice. Watch this if you add a Google-first signup path that leaves the column NULL.
Google sign-in links by email: an existing email/password user who signs in with Google gets google_id attached (findOrCreateUser in google.go). Unverified Google emails are rejected with 403.

OAuth CSRF state is a random 32-byte value in an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie named oauth_state, compared to the ?state param in Callback. The Sheets flow in the datasource domain uses the same pattern with different cookie names.
The Google callback ends by redirecting to FRONTEND_URL/auth/callback?token=<jwt> — the token travels in a URL, which is why the frontend page immediately stores it and replaces the URL.
JWT_SECRET, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET/REDIRECT_URL come from env; main.go log.Fatals if JWT_SECRET is missing but NOT if the Google vars are missing (Google sign-in just fails at runtime).
